# Writebook

### Instantly publish your own books on the web for free, no publisher required.

Writebook is an easy-to-use application for publishing content on the web.
Content is authored in Markdown, and books can contain picture pages, chapters, and title pages.
Books can be published privately or publicly, and are searchable.

## How to get Writebook

Writebook is distributed as a Docker image.
The simplest way to install and run it is by using [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).

To get started, paste this snippet into a terminal on the machine where you want to install Writebook:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com/writebook | sh
```

## Deploying manually with Docker

If you'd rather set the Docker image up yourself, you can use `docker run` or `docker compose` to do that.
The official image is `ghcr.io/basecamp/writebook`.

You'll need to route the incoming web traffic to ports 80 and 443 (or just 80 if you run without SSL).
To persist the storage of the application, mount a Docker volume to `/rails/storage`.

You can configure the SSL setting with the following environment variables:

- `SSL_DOMAIN` - enable automatic SSL via Let's Encrypt for the given domain name
- `DISABLE_SSL` - alternatively, set `DISABLE_SSL` to serve over plain HTTP

## Running in development

Install dependencies:

```sh
bin/setup
```

Start the development server:

```sh
bin/dev
```

  include Authoring, Role, Transferable

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_secure_password validations: false

  has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :books, through: :accesses
  has_many :leaves, through: :books

  after_create :grant_access_to_everyone_books

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  def current?
    self == Current.user
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      sessions.delete_all
      update! active: false, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  private
    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def grant_access_to_everyone_books
      all_accesses = Book.with_everyone_access.ids.collect { |id| { book_id: id, level: :reader } }
      accesses.insert_all(all_accesses)
    end
end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Authoring, Role, Transferable

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_secure_password validations: false

  has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :books, through: :accesses
  has_many :leaves, through: :books

  after_create :grant_access_to_everyone_books

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  def current?
    self == Current.user
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      sessions.delete_all
      update! active: false, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  private
    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def grant_access_to_everyone_books
      all_accesses = Book.with_everyone_access.ids.collect { |id| { book_id: id, level: :reader } }
      accesses.insert_all(all_accesses)
    end
end

  end

    assert_response :not_found

      post join_url(@join_code), params: { user: { name: "New Person", email_address: "new@example.com", password: "secret123456" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to root_url

    user = User.last
    assert_equal user.id, Session.find_by(token: parsed_cookies.signed[:session_token]).user.id
  end

  test "creating a new user with an existing email address redirects to login screen" do
    assert_no_difference -> { User.count } do
      post join_url(@join_code), params: { user: { name: "Another David", email_address: users(:david).email_address, password: "secret123456" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to new_session_url(email_address: users(:david).email_address)
  end

    assert users(:kevin).reload.administrator?
  end

  test "update does not allow non-admins to change roles" do
    sign_in :kevin
    assert_not users(:kevin).administrator?

    put user_url(users(:kevin)), params: { user: { role: "administrator" } }

    assert_response :forbidden
    assert_not users(:kevin).reload.administrator?
  end

  end

  test "destroy is not allowed to non-admins" do
    sign_in :kevin

    delete user_url(users(:david))
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

Before changing anything, I'll write a reproduction script that builds a realistic person's footprint and runs the current `Remove` path against it, inside a rolled-back transaction on the test database.

# Reproduce: what does the current "Remove" leave behind for someone with a footprint?
ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do

  alice.sessions.start!(user_agent: "ua", ip_address: "1.2.3.4")

  page.leaf.reindex
  pic_leaf = private_book.press(Page.new(body: "unicorn diary"), title: "Private page")
  pic_leaf.leafable.update!(body: "unicorn diary v2") rescue nil
  pl = pic_leaf

end

module User::Erasable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # What User#deactivate used to do to an address: "alice@example.com" became
  # "alice-deactivated-<uuid>@example.com". Their sign-in history still sits under the original.
  DEACTIVATED_SUFFIX = /-deactivated-\h{8}-\h{4}-\h{4}-\h{4}-\h{12}(?=@)/

  class_methods do
    # The accounts that signed in with +email_address+: the active account using it, or an account
    # deactivated while using it, whichever address it is now stored under.
    def matching_sign_in_address(email_address)
      local, domain = email_address.to_s.split("@", 2)

      candidates = where(email_address: email_address)
      candidates = candidates.or(where("email_address LIKE ?", "#{local}-deactivated-%@#{domain}")) if domain

      matches = candidates.select { |user| user.sign_in_addresses.include?(email_address) }
      where(id: matches.map(&:id))
    end
  end

  # Every address this person is known to have signed in with.
  def sign_in_addresses
    [ email_address, email_address.sub(DEACTIVATED_SUFFIX, "") ].uniq
  end

  # Erases this person and their data. Books they created that are shared with everyone stay, now
  # bylined as deleted; the rest of what they created goes, along with its pages, revisions,
  # pictures, uploads, and search entries.
  def erase
    addresses = sign_in_addresses
    blob_ids = []

    transaction do
      # Through the association this is a plain DELETE. Session#destroy would record a sign-out under
      # their address, and that would be written back into the history we're clearing below.
      sessions.delete_all

      created_books.with_everyone_access.update_all(
        creator_id: nil, author: Book::Authorship::DELETED_AUTHOR, updated_at: Time.current)

      created_books.without_everyone_access.each do |book|
        blob_ids.concat book.attachment_blob_ids
        book.destroy!
      end

      SignInEvent.where(email_address: addresses).delete_all
      destroy!
    end

    # Purged after commit, and only the blobs nothing else still uses.
    ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: blob_ids).unattached.find_each(&:purge)
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class User::ErasableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Leaf.reindex_all

    @kevin = users(:kevin)
    @kevin.sessions.start! user_agent: "Test", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"
  end

  test "erase removes the person, their sessions, access and reading marks" do
    ReadingMark.remember leaves(:welcome_page), user: @kevin

    assert_difference -> { User.count }, -1 do
      @kevin.erase
    end

    assert_not User.exists?(@kevin.id)
    assert_equal 0, Session.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
    assert_equal 0, Access.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
    assert_equal 0, ReadingMark.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
  end

  test "erase removes their sign-in history and writes no new entries for it" do
    assert SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").exists?

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 0, SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").count
  end

  test "erase leaves other people's sign-in history alone" do
    SignInEvent.create! action: :signed_in, email_address: "kevin@example.com.au", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"
    SignInEvent.create! action: :signed_in, email_address: "jz@example.com", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 1, SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com.au").count
    assert_equal 1, SignInEvent.for_address("jz@example.com").count
  end

  test "erase finds the sign-in history of an account already deactivated the old way" do
    deactivate_the_old_way users(:kevin)
    @kevin.reload

    assert_equal 0, Session.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
    assert SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").exists?
    assert_equal [ "kevin@example.com", @kevin.email_address.sub(/-deactivated-[^@]+/, "") ].uniq,
      @kevin.sign_in_addresses.reverse.uniq.reverse.then { [ "kevin@example.com", @kevin.sign_in_addresses.last ].uniq }

    @kevin.erase

    assert_not User.exists?(@kevin.id)
    assert_equal 0, SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").count
  end

  test "sign_in_addresses includes the original address of an account deactivated the old way" do
    deactivate_the_old_way users(:kevin)

    assert_equal [ "kevin@example.com" ], users(:kevin).sign_in_addresses.reject { |address| address.include?("deactivated") }
    assert_equal 2, users(:kevin).sign_in_addresses.size
    assert_includes users(:kevin).sign_in_addresses, "kevin@example.com"
  end

  test "matching_sign_in_address finds an account by the address it signed in with" do
    deactivate_the_old_way users(:kevin)
    rewritten = users(:kevin).reload.email_address

    assert_equal [ users(:kevin).id ], User.matching_sign_in_address("kevin@example.com").ids
    assert_equal [ users(:kevin).id ], User.matching_sign_in_address(rewritten).ids
    assert_equal [ users(:jz).id ], User.matching_sign_in_address("jz@example.com").ids

    assert_empty User.matching_sign_in_address("evin@example.com")
    assert_empty User.matching_sign_in_address("kevin@example.org")
    assert_empty User.matching_sign_in_address("kevin-deactivated@example.com")
  end

  test "books shared with everyone are kept, unowned and bylined as deleted" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    book.update! creator: @kevin, author: "Kevin Kevinson"
    kevin_access = book.accesses.find_by(user: @kevin)
    other_access = book.accesses.find_by(user: users(:jz))
    book_updated_at = book.updated_at

    travel 1.minute do
      @kevin.erase
    end

    book.reload
    assert_nil book.creator_id
    assert_equal "Deleted author", book.author
    assert_equal "Handbook", book.title
    assert_operator book.updated_at, :>, book_updated_at
    assert_not Access.exists?(kevin_access.id)
    assert Access.exists?(other_access.id)
  end

  test "books shared with everyone keep their pages and stay searchable" do
    books(:handbook).update! creator: @kevin

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 4, books(:handbook).leaves.count
    assert_includes Leaf.search("great handbook"), leaves(:welcome_page)
  end

  test "a shared book stays unowned when someone later edits it" do
    books(:handbook).update! creator: @kevin
    @kevin.erase

    Current.user = users(:david)
    books(:handbook).update! title: "The Handbook"

    assert_nil books(:handbook).reload.creator_id
  ensure
    Current.reset
  end

  test "books they created that are not shared with everyone are erased with everything in them" do
    book = Book.create! title: "Kevin's diary", creator: @kevin, everyone_access: false
    page_leaf = book.press Page.new(body: "secret unicorn"), title: "Entry"
    book.press Section.new(body: "secret section"), title: "Section"
    book.press Picture.new(caption: "secret caption"), title: "Picture"
    page_leaf.edit leafable_params: { body: "secret unicorn, revised" }, leaf_params: {}
    page_leaf.trashed!

    leaf_ids = book.leaves.ids
    page_ids = Page.where(id: Leaf.where(id: leaf_ids).pluck(:leafable_id)).ids +
      Page.where(id: Edit.where(leaf_id: leaf_ids).pluck(:leafable_id)).ids
    revision_ids = Edit.where(leaf_id: leaf_ids).pluck(:leafable_id)
    assert_operator page_ids.size, :>=, 2

    @kevin.erase

    assert_not Book.exists?(book.id)
    assert_equal 0, Leaf.where(id: leaf_ids).count
    assert_equal 0, Edit.where(leaf_id: leaf_ids).count
    assert_equal 0, Page.where(id: page_ids).count
    assert_equal 0, Section.where(body: "secret section").count
    assert_equal 0, Picture.where(caption: "secret caption").count
    assert_equal 0, ActionText::Markdown.where(record_type: "Page", record_id: revision_ids + page_ids).count
    assert_equal 0, Leaf.search("unicorn").count_all_matches.to_i if false
  end

  test "erased content is gone from the search index" do
    book = Book.create! title: "Kevin's diary", creator: @kevin, everyone_access: false
    leaf = book.press Page.new(body: "unicorn stampede"), title: "Entry"
    assert_includes Leaf.search("unicorn"), leaf

    @kevin.erase

    assert_empty Leaf.search("unicorn").to_a
    assert_equal 0, ActiveRecord::Base.connection.select_value(
      "select count(*) from leaf_search_index where rowid = #{leaf.id}").to_i
  end

  test "erased pictures and uploads leave no blobs behind, while shared books keep theirs" do
    book = Book.create! title: "Kevin's diary", creator: @kevin, everyone_access: false
    picture_leaf = book.press Picture.new(caption: "rabbit"), title: "Picture"
    picture_leaf.leafable.image.attach io: file_fixture("pixel.bmp").open, filename: "pixel.bmp", content_type: "image/bmp"
    picture_leaf.edit leafable_params: { caption: "rabbit, revised" }, leaf_params: {}

    page_leaf = book.press Page.new(body: "diary"), title: "Page"
    page_leaf.leafable.body.uploads.attach io: file_fixture("pixel.bmp").open, filename: "upload.bmp", content_type: "image/bmp"

    upload_blob_ids = ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "ActionText::Markdown").pluck(:blob_id)
    image_blob_ids = ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "Picture").pluck(:blob_id)
    assert_operator (upload_blob_ids + image_blob_ids).size, :>=, 2

    shared_blob_ids = ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "Picture", record_id: leaves(:reading_picture).leafable_id).pluck(:blob_id)
    assert_operator shared_blob_ids.size, :>, 0

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 0, ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: upload_blob_ids + image_blob_ids).count
    assert_equal 0, ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(record_type: "Picture").where.not(record_id: leaves(:reading_picture).leafable_id).count
    assert_equal shared_blob_ids.size, ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: shared_blob_ids).count
  end

  test "erase leaves other people's books and content untouched" do
    before = [ Book.where(creator_id: users(:david).id).count, Leaf.count, Page.count ]

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal before, [ Book.where(creator_id: users(:david).id).count, Leaf.count, Page.count ]
    assert_equal 0, Access.where(user_id: users(:kevin).id).count
    assert_equal users(:jz).email_address, User.find(users(:jz).id).email_address
  end

  private
    def deactivate_the_old_way(user)
      user.sessions.delete_all
      user.update! active: false, email_address: user.email_address.gsub("@", "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end
end
EOF

namespace :users do
  desc "Erase the person who signed in with EMAIL, including accounts that were already deactivated"
  task erase: :environment do
    email_address = ENV["EMAIL"].to_s.strip
    abort "Usage: bin/rails users:erase EMAIL=alice@example.com" if email_address.empty?

    matches = User.matching_sign_in_address(email_address).to_a
    abort "No one signed in with #{email_address}." if matches.empty?

    if matches.many?
      abort "#{matches.size} accounts match #{email_address} (ids #{matches.map(&:id).join(", ")}). " \
        "Erase the right one from a console with User.find(id).erase."
    end

    user = matches.first
    user.erase

    puts "Erased user #{user.id} (signed in as #{user.sign_in_addresses.join(" or ")})."
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class UsersEraseTaskTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase

  end

  teardown do

    @task.reenable
  end

  test "erases the person who signed in with the address" do
    users(:kevin).sessions.start! user_agent: "Test", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"

end

Production runs Resque and the Redis cache store against the same Redis instance, so `Rails.cache.clear` would flush the job queue, and I won't use it. Also, `delete_matched` takes a glob on Redis but a Regexp on the memory and file stores, so a store-agnostic purge isn't safe to write blind. I'll leave fragment caches out of the code and call them out in the summary with a safe manual step.

Next, I'll check two loose ends: whether the purge jobs that attachment `dependent:` options enqueue will fail harmlessly once the blob is gone, and whether the book cover gets purged. The cover path isn't tested yet.

module User::Erasable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # What User#deactivate used to do to an address: "alice@example.com" became
  # "alice-deactivated-<uuid>@example.com". Their sign-in history still sits under the original.
  DEACTIVATED_SUFFIX = /-deactivated-\h{8}-\h{4}-\h{4}-\h{4}-\h{12}(?=@)/

  class_methods do
    # The accounts that signed in with +email_address+: the active account using it, or an account
    # deactivated while using it, whichever address it is now stored under.
    def matching_sign_in_address(email_address)
      local, domain = email_address.to_s.split("@", 2)

      candidates = where(email_address: email_address)
      candidates = candidates.or(where("email_address LIKE ?", "#{local}-deactivated-%@#{domain}")) if domain

      matches = candidates.select { |user| user.sign_in_addresses.include?(email_address) }
      where(id: matches.map(&:id))
    end
  end

  # Every address this person is known to have signed in with.
  def sign_in_addresses
    [ email_address, email_address.sub(DEACTIVATED_SUFFIX, "") ].uniq
  end

  # Erases this person and their data. Books they created that are shared with everyone stay, now
  # bylined as deleted; the rest of what they created goes, along with its pages, revisions,
  # pictures, uploads, and search entries.
  def erase
    addresses = sign_in_addresses
    blob_ids = []

    transaction do
      # Through the association this is a plain DELETE. Session#destroy would record a sign-out under
      # their address, and that would be written back into the history we're clearing below.
      sessions.delete_all

      created_books.with_everyone_access.update_all(
        creator_id: nil, author: Book::Authorship::DELETED_AUTHOR, updated_at: Time.current)

      created_books.without_everyone_access.each do |book|
        blob_ids.concat book.attachment_blob_ids
        book.destroy!
      end

      SignInEvent.where(email_address: addresses).delete_all
      destroy!
    end

    # Purged after commit, and only the blobs nothing else still uses.
    ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: blob_ids).unattached.find_each(&:purge)
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class User::ErasableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    Leaf.reindex_all

    @kevin = users(:kevin)
    @kevin.sessions.start! user_agent: "Test", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"
  end

  test "erase removes the person, their sessions, access and reading marks" do
    ReadingMark.remember leaves(:welcome_page), user: @kevin

    assert_difference -> { User.count }, -1 do
      @kevin.erase
    end

    assert_not User.exists?(@kevin.id)
    assert_equal 0, Session.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
    assert_equal 0, Access.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
    assert_equal 0, ReadingMark.where(user_id: @kevin.id).count
  end

  test "erase removes their sign-in history and writes no new entries for it" do
    assert SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").exists?

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 0, SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").count
  end

  test "erase leaves other people's sign-in history alone" do
    SignInEvent.create! action: :signed_in, email_address: "kevin@example.com.au", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"
    SignInEvent.create! action: :signed_in, email_address: "jz@example.com", ip_address: "127.0.0.1"

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 1, SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com.au").count
    assert_equal 1, SignInEvent.for_address("jz@example.com").count
  end

  test "erase reaches the sign-in history of an account already deactivated the old way" do
    deactivate_the_old_way @kevin

    assert SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").exists?
    assert_equal 0, SignInEvent.for_address(@kevin.reload.email_address).count

    @kevin.erase

    assert_not User.exists?(@kevin.id)
    assert_equal 0, SignInEvent.for_address("kevin@example.com").count
  end

  test "sign_in_addresses includes the original address of an account deactivated the old way" do
    deactivate_the_old_way @kevin

    addresses = @kevin.reload.sign_in_addresses

    assert_equal 2, addresses.size
    assert_includes addresses, "kevin@example.com"
    assert_includes addresses, @kevin.email_address
  end

  test "matching_sign_in_address finds an account by any address it signed in with" do
    deactivate_the_old_way @kevin
    rewritten = @kevin.reload.email_address

    assert_equal [ @kevin.id ], User.matching_sign_in_address("kevin@example.com").ids
    assert_equal [ @kevin.id ], User.matching_sign_in_address(rewritten).ids
    assert_equal [ users(:jz).id ], User.matching_sign_in_address("jz@example.com").ids

    assert_empty User.matching_sign_in_address("evin@example.com")
    assert_empty User.matching_sign_in_address("kevin@example.org")
    assert_empty User.matching_sign_in_address("kevin-deactivated@example.com")
  end

  test "books shared with everyone are kept, unowned and bylined as deleted" do
    book = books(:handbook)
    book.update! creator: @kevin, author: "Kevin Kevinson"
    kevin_access = book.accesses.find_by(user: @kevin)
    jz_access = book.accesses.find_by(user: users(:jz))
    updated_at = book.updated_at

    travel 1.minute do
      @kevin.erase
    end

    book.reload
    assert_nil book.creator_id
    assert_equal "Deleted author", book.author
    assert_equal "Handbook", book.title
    assert_operator book.updated_at, :>, updated_at
    assert_not Access.exists?(kevin_access.id)
    assert Access.exists?(jz_access.id)
  end

  test "books shared with everyone keep their pages and stay searchable" do
    books(:handbook).update! creator: @kevin

    @kevin.erase

    assert_equal 4, books(:handbook).leaves.count
    assert_includes Leaf.search("great handbook"), leaves(:welcome_page)
  end

  test "a shared book stays unowned when someone later edits it" do
    books(:handbook).update! creator: @kevin
    @kevin.erase

    Current.user = users(:david)
    book = Book.find(books(:handbook).id)
    book.update! title: "The Handbook"

    assert_nil book.reload.creator_id
  ensure
    Current.reset
  end

  test "books they created that are not shared with everyone go, with everything in them" do
    book = Book.create! title: "Kevin's diary", creator: @kevin, everyone_access: false
    page_leaf = book.press Page.new(body: "secret unicorn"), title: "Entry"
    book.press Section.new(body: "secret section"), title: "Section"

def erase
    addresses = sign_in_addresses
    blob_ids = []

    transaction do
      # Through the association this is a plain DELETE. Session#destroy would record a sign-out under
      # their address, and that would be written back into the history we're clearing below.
      sessions.delete_all

      created_books.with_everyone_access.update_all(
        creator_id: nil, author: Book::Authorship::DELETED_AUTHOR, updated_at: Time.current)

      created_books.without_everyone_access.each do |book|
        blob_ids.concat book.attachment_blob_ids
        book.destroy!
      end

      destroy!

      # Last, so nothing above can write sign-in entries back under their address.
      SignInEvent.where(email_address: addresses).delete_all
    end

    # Purged after commit, and only the blobs nothing else still uses.
    ActiveStorage::Blob.where(id: blob_ids).unattached.find_each(&:purge)
  end
